papers.full_text: AbstractObjectiveTo conduct a three-year cervical cancer screen in Zhejiang, Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia and analyse clinical and population data to identify possible improvements to the screening protocol.MethodsA standard protocol including human papillomavirus (HPV) detection, cytology test, colposcopy, and histopathology inspection was adapted for the screening. Additional HPV genotyping was performed for participants in Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia.Results12,086 women were included in this study, and 178 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) were identified. Detailed analyses on features of age, region, ethnicity, and origin showed a notable correlation between age strata and high-grade CIN rates. Moreover, apart from HPV16/18, other HPV types such as HPV33, HPV52, and HPV58 were found to be enriched in high-grade CIN cases, as was repeat positivity.ConclusionsOur results suggest that age, HPV16, and ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) are prominent exploratory predictors for CIN2+ detection, and HPV33, 52, and 58 may pose higher risks than other non-HPV16/18 types. Future studies incorporating prospective effectiveness and health-economic evaluation are required to validate the clinical utility of these predictors.Keywords: age, cervical cancer screening, genotyping, HPV, repeat positivity 2.Methodology2.1.Study population and screening protocolThis research was conducted in 4 provinces (including a municipality): Sichuan, Zhejiang, Inner Mongolia and Beijing. Women between 20 and 65 years of age with a history of sexual activity were recruited for screening. The exclusion criteria were: (a) a previous diagnosis of cervical cancer; (b) current chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or both; (c) being pregnant or within 8 weeks postpartum; (d) a history of pelvic radiotherapy or chemotherapy, cervical resection within 12 months before the study, or total hysterectomy; and (e) a history of HPV vaccination. A 3-year screening and follow-up protocol, illustrated in Figure 1, was implemented. In brief, participants underwent routine testing (pooled detection of 18 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) types with separate identification of HPV16/18) and TCTs at the beginning of screening and were assigned to colposcopy assessment, next-year follow-up, or third-year follow-up according to the results. At the next-year follow-up, TCTs were performed, and participants with abnormal cytology were referred to colposcopy, while those with a TCT result negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM) were scheduled for another follow-up before the third year. At the third-year follow-up, HPV genotyping and TCTs were performed, and participants with a positive HPV result or abnormal cytology were referred to colposcopy. Participants who underwent colposcopy had histological samples taken for pathological diagnosis. Those diagnosed with CIN2 or worse (CIN2+) left the study and were treated accordingly, while the others continued to the next follow-up until the end of the study. Extended genotyping was available for all Sichuan participants, for participants enrolled during the last three screening rounds in Beijing and Inner Mongolia, and for none in Zhejiang. This was an operational, site- and round-dependent implementation rather than a random sample of the full cohort. Repeat positivity was defined as positive results at two consecutive available HPV tests. Because routine HPV testing was not performed in Years 1 and 2, and extended genotyping was not uniformly conducted at baseline, same-genotype continuity was not consistently demonstrable. Therefore, clearance, reinfection, new infection, and true persistence cannot be distinguished, and this measure must not be interpreted as guideline-defined persistent infection.Figure 1Process of cervical cancer screening.Flowchart of the three-year cervical screening pathway. Cervical exfoliated cells undergo HPV genotyping and ThinPrep cytology testing (TCT). Depending on baseline results, participants proceed to first-year TCT, return for HPV and TCT testing in year three, or undergo colposcopy and histopathology. Abnormal cytology during annual follow-up prompts colposcopy; HPV positivity or abnormal cytology in year three also prompts colposcopy. Histopathology showing CIN2 or worse leads to “Trial end.” Participants with normal final cytology or histopathology no worse than CIN1 reach “Follow-up end.” Arrows connect the test results to subsequent assessments and endpoints.2.2.Sample collectionCervical exfoliated cells were collected by gynaecologists using collectors (Hologic Inc., Marlborough, MA, USA) and preserved in PreservCyt Solution (Hologic Inc., Marlborough, MA, USA) for TCT and HPV genotyping within 48 h.2.3.HPV detectionDNA was extracted using DNA extraction kits (Yaneng BIOscience (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, Guangdong, China), and HPV DNA was routinely tested using HPV DNA detection and HPV16/18 genotyping kits (PCR-fluorescence probing; Yaneng BIOscience (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, Guangdong, China), which can detect 18 hrHPV types in a pooled assay (16, 18, 26, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 53, 56, 58, 59, 66, 68, 73, and 82) and separately genotype HPV16 and HPV18. For all extended type-specific genotyping, HPV DNA detection and genotyping kits (PCR-reverse dot hybridisation; Yaneng BIOscience (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, Guangdong, China) were used. The detection experiments were conducted strictly according to the manufacturer’s instructions.2.4.Liquid-based cytologyExfoliated cell cytology was examined by experienced pathologists according to the 2014 Bethesda System and characterised as follows: (a) negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM); (b) atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US); (c) atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (ASC-H); (d) atypical glandular cells (AGC); (e) low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL); and (f) high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL).2.5.Colposcopy and histopathologyColposcopies were performed by gynaecologists, and biopsies were performed when visible lesions were found. The histopathological examinations were then performed to establish final diagnoses of <CIN1, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grades 1 to 3, and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC).2.6.Statistical analysis and modellingStatistical analyses were performed using Python 3.6 with the NumPy module. Modelling, including cross-validation and permutations, was performed using the scikit-learn module. Before being entered into the models, features were coded as unordered factors, except for age, which was coded numerically. The random forest (RF) models were constructed with default parameters and 100 trees. Permutations were performed 10 times to calculate the permutation importance of each feature. The shap package in Python was used to calculate Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) values (Lundberg and Lee, 2017) and perform further analyses and visualisation of these values. It should be noted that the full baseline dataset was used for model fitting and importance estimation; there was no independent test set. Therefore, RF/SHAP results were considered exploratory associations, not causal effects. For age adjustment, direct standardisation was used across five prespecified age strata (<30, 30–39, 40–49, 50–59, and ≥60 years). The standard population was the age distribution of all 12,086 participants. For each subgroup, the age-standardised CIN2+ rate was calculated as Σ(wi × ri), where wi is the proportion of the full cohort in age stratum i and ri is the subgroup-specific CIN2+ rate in that stratum. To evaluate differences in CIN2+ rates between subgroups, a global Pearson chi-square test was used to compare the four regional Han groups. Prespecified two-sided Fisher’s exact tests were applied for pairwise comparisons where expected counts were low. All statistical tests were two-sided, and P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Supplementary materialThe Supplementary Material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fcimb.2026.1920297/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials 3.Results3.1.Cervical screening profileOverall, 12,086 women aged 20 to 65 years, with an average age of 44.83 ± 8.93 years, from four different provinces or municipalities were involved in this study (Table 1). The majority of participants were Han; ethnic minority groups with more than 50 participants included Yi, Mongol, Hui, and Man, while the remaining minorities were grouped as “other” and were not listed in detail. According to information on the participants’ personal IDs, more women were born in rural areas than in urban areas. At first enrolment, the positive rate for HPV detection was 14.81%, the abnormal rate for TCTs was 7.84%, and 93 patients were diagnosed with CIN2+ and referred for further treatment (Table 2). Another 85 patients were diagnosed with high-grade CIN or SCC during follow-up screening and left the study for treatment. The overall cumulative three-year CIN2+ rate of the cohort was 1.47% (178/12,086), while the baseline rate was 0.77% (93/12,086). CIN2+ rates among participants who underwent colposcopy at specific time points were 16.03% (93/580) at baseline, 17.36% (21/121) in Year 1, 7.27% (12/165) in Year 2, and 4.62% (52/1,126) in Year 3, respectively. HPV was detected only at enrolment and in the third year according to the screening protocol, but additional HPV genotyping tests were performed for participants in Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia, and the results are presented in the following sections.Table 1Participant population profile.CategorySubgroupCountsProportion (%) Total 12086100.00% Age (-, 30)5364.43%[30, 40)305125.24%[40, 50)453537.52%[50, 60)340228.15%[60, -)5624.65% Ethnic Han1089790.16%Yi7366.09%Mongol2932.42%Hui730.60%Man640.53%Other230.19% Region Zhejiang302825.05%InnerMongolia277422.95%Beijing310325.67%Sichuan318126.32% Origin Urban422734.97%Rural785965.03%Table 2Overview of cervical cancer screening results.VariableBaselineYear 1Year 2Year 3HPVHPV-10296Not performedNot performed8155HPV16224Not performedNot performed88HPV18108Not performedNot performed40HPV16/187Not performedNot performed0hrHPV1451Not performedNot performed911Total12086 (100.00%)//9194 (100.00%)TCTNILM11138169417258727ASC-US687106187380ASC-H7610924AGC29538LSIL112291946HSIL44535Total TCT tested12086 (100.00%)1849 (100.00%)1946 (100.00%)9190 (100.00%)Histopathology<CIN137372129783CIN11142824291CIN2409937CIN35212314SCC1001CIN2+ subtotal93211252Total580 (100.00%)121 (100.00%)165 (100.00%)1126 (100.00%)3.2.Population feature analysisRates of CIN2+ were investigated in different population groups. Only data from the first screen were used in this analysis, as follow-up was performed in a subgroup of the same population. Population features including age, origin (urban/rural born), ethnicity, and location (province or municipality) of testing, and clinical features derived from HPV test and TCT results were considered as features potentially associated with CIN2+ rates. As only 93 cases of CIN2+ were identified at the first screen, this number of positive cases was insufficient to perform robust statistical analyses on these eight features. Therefore, classification random forest (RF) models were used to assist the analysis by estimating the importance of these features.As the main aim was to estimate feature importance rather than to train a general model, the full baseline dataset was used for model fitting and importance estimation; there was no independent test set. This design creates risks of overfitting and optimistic importance estimates. Therefore, RF/SHAP results were considered exploratory associations, not causal effects. A 10-fold cross-validation resulted in an average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.884 with a standard deviation of 0.078, indicating that the model was able to capture relations between these features and the CIN2+ results without excessive overfitting. Feature importance was assessed using permutation-induced changes in prediction accuracy and SHAP values. Feature importance results are shown in Figure 2, where permutation importance, expressed as decreases in accuracy, is presented in Figure 2a; SHAP importance, expressed as the mean absolute SHAP value, is presented in Figure 2b; and the corresponding distributions of SHAP values across features are presented in Figure 2c. Although the order of importance varied between estimation methods, it is clear that TCT results, age, and HPV16 infections are strong exploratory indicators of CIN2+ diagnoses. Notably, the difference between the SHAP values for age (0.12) and HPV16 (0.13) was negligible, indicating that both age and HPV16 serve as important predictors with comparable predictive contributions. Meanwhile, participants’ origin, ethnicity, and HPV18 infection had lower estimated importance. It is worth noting that reliable estimates of the importance of HPV infection-related features would be largely affected by the number of infections with the relevant HPV type, since rare cases could not provide enough information to establish relationships within the models. Therefore, infections with other non-16/18 hrHPV types, including some uncommon types, were grouped into a single feature. Among the population-related features, age appeared to be the most important, followed by region and origin, while ethnicity was suggested by the models to be the least important. The SHAP value distribution of the age feature (Figure 2c) exhibited a more complicated nonlinear association with CIN2+ than those of the TCT and HPV-related features, requiring more detailed investigation.Figure 2Feature importance estimated by permutation and SHAP. (a) Permutation importance calculated as the mean reduction in accuracy, with error bars representing the standard deviations over 10 repeats. (b) SHAP importance as the mean absolute SHAP value for different classes, and (c) the corresponding distributions of SHAP values across different features. “Non-16/18 hrHPV” represents infection with high-risk HPV types other than HPV16/18. The “origin” feature represents the urbanisation level of participants’ families at birth.Figure containing three panels. Panel a shows a horizontal bar chart of features ranked by reduced accuracy, with TCT and Age as top features. Panel b displays a horizontal stacked bar chart of mean SHAP values, illustrating the average impact on model output magnitude for each feature, separated by >CIN2 and ≤CIN2 outcomes. Panel c presents a SHAP summary plot with feature values color-coded from high (pink) to low (blue), showing the distribution and influence of each feature on model output.To verify the feature-importance estimates produced by the models, CIN2+ rates were examined in subgroups separated by region, origin, and ethnicity. Only subgroups with populations over 200 were investigated in detail, as large errors may be introduced given that the overall CIN2+ rate was merely 1.47% (see Supplementary Table 1 for detailed data). full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractObjectiveTo conduct a three-year cervical cancer screen in Zhejiang, Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia and analyse clinical and population data to identify possible improvements to the screening protocol.MethodsA standard protocol including human papillomavirus (HPV) detection, cytology test, colposcopy, and histopathology inspection was adapted for the screening. Additional HPV genotyping was performed for participants in Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia.Results12,086 women were included in this study, and 178 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) were identified. Detailed analyses on features of age, region, ethnicity, and origin showed a notable correlation between age strata and high-grade CIN rates. Moreover, apart from HPV16/18, other HPV types such as HPV33, HPV52, and HPV58 were found to be enriched in high-grade CIN cases, as was repeat positivity.ConclusionsOur results suggest that age, HPV16, and ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) are prominent exploratory predictors for CIN2+ detection, and HPV33, 52, and 58 may pose higher risks than other non-HPV16/18 types. Future studies incorporating prospective effectiveness and health-economic evaluation are required to validate the clinical utility of these predictors.Keywords: age, cervical cancer screening, genotyping, HPV, repeat positivity
full_text_sections.methods: 2.Methodology2.1.Study population and screening protocolThis research was conducted in 4 provinces (including a municipality): Sichuan, Zhejiang, Inner Mongolia and Beijing. Women between 20 and 65 years of age with a history of sexual activity were recruited for screening. The exclusion criteria were: (a) a previous diagnosis of cervical cancer; (b) current chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or both; (c) being pregnant or within 8 weeks postpartum; (d) a history of pelvic radiotherapy or chemotherapy, cervical resection within 12 months before the study, or total hysterectomy; and (e) a history of HPV vaccination. A 3-year screening and follow-up protocol, illustrated in Figure 1, was implemented. In brief, participants underwent routine testing (pooled detection of 18 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) types with separate identification of HPV16/18) and TCTs at the beginning of screening and were assigned to colposcopy assessment, next-year follow-up, or third-year follow-up according to the results. At the next-year follow-up, TCTs were performed, and participants with abnormal cytology were referred to colposcopy, while those with a TCT result negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM) were scheduled for another follow-up before the third year. At the third-year follow-up, HPV genotyping and TCTs were performed, and participants with a positive HPV result or abnormal cytology were referred to colposcopy. Participants who underwent colposcopy had histological samples taken for pathological diagnosis. Those diagnosed with CIN2 or worse (CIN2+) left the study and were treated accordingly, while the others continued to the next follow-up until the end of the study. Extended genotyping was available for all Sichuan participants, for participants enrolled during the last three screening rounds in Beijing and Inner Mongolia, and for none in Zhejiang. This was an operational, site- and round-dependent implementation rather than a random sample of the full cohort. Repeat positivity was defined as positive results at two consecutive available HPV tests. Because routine HPV testing was not performed in Years 1 and 2, and extended genotyping was not uniformly conducted at baseline, same-genotype continuity was not consistently demonstrable. Therefore, clearance, reinfection, new infection, and true persistence cannot be distinguished, and this measure must not be interpreted as guideline-defined persistent infection.Figure 1Process of cervical cancer screening.Flowchart of the three-year cervical screening pathway. Cervical exfoliated cells undergo HPV genotyping and ThinPrep cytology testing (TCT). Depending on baseline results, participants proceed to first-year TCT, return for HPV and TCT testing in year three, or undergo colposcopy and histopathology. Abnormal cytology during annual follow-up prompts colposcopy; HPV positivity or abnormal cytology in year three also prompts colposcopy. Histopathology showing CIN2 or worse leads to “Trial end.” Participants with normal final cytology or histopathology no worse than CIN1 reach “Follow-up end.” Arrows connect the test results to subsequent assessments and endpoints.2.2.Sample collectionCervical exfoliated cells were collected by gynaecologists using collectors (Hologic Inc., Marlborough, MA, USA) and preserved in PreservCyt Solution (Hologic Inc., Marlborough, MA, USA) for TCT and HPV genotyping within 48 h.2.3.HPV detectionDNA was extracted using DNA extraction kits (Yaneng BIOscience (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, Guangdong, China), and HPV DNA was routinely tested using HPV DNA detection and HPV16/18 genotyping kits (PCR-fluorescence probing; Yaneng BIOscience (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, Guangdong, China), which can detect 18 hrHPV types in a pooled assay (16, 18, 26, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 53, 56, 58, 59, 66, 68, 73, and 82) and separately genotype HPV16 and HPV18. For all extended type-specific genotyping, HPV DNA detection and genotyping kits (PCR-reverse dot hybridisation; Yaneng BIOscience (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, Guangdong, China) were used. The detection experiments were conducted strictly according to the manufacturer’s instructions.2.4.Liquid-based cytologyExfoliated cell cytology was examined by experienced pathologists according to the 2014 Bethesda System and characterised as follows: (a) negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM); (b) atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US); (c) atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (ASC-H); (d) atypical glandular cells (AGC); (e) low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL); and (f) high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL).2.5.Colposcopy and histopathologyColposcopies were performed by gynaecologists, and biopsies were performed when visible lesions were found. The histopathological examinations were then performed to establish final diagnoses of <CIN1, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grades 1 to 3, and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC).2.6.Statistical analysis and modellingStatistical analyses were performed using Python 3.6 with the NumPy module. Modelling, including cross-validation and permutations, was performed using the scikit-learn module. Before being entered into the models, features were coded as unordered factors, except for age, which was coded numerically. The random forest (RF) models were constructed with default parameters and 100 trees. Permutations were performed 10 times to calculate the permutation importance of each feature. The shap package in Python was used to calculate Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) values (Lundberg and Lee, 2017) and perform further analyses and visualisation of these values. It should be noted that the full baseline dataset was used for model fitting and importance estimation; there was no independent test set. Therefore, RF/SHAP results were considered exploratory associations, not causal effects. For age adjustment, direct standardisation was used across five prespecified age strata (<30, 30–39, 40–49, 50–59, and ≥60 years). The standard population was the age distribution of all 12,086 participants. For each subgroup, the age-standardised CIN2+ rate was calculated as Σ(wi × ri), where wi is the proportion of the full cohort in age stratum i and ri is the subgroup-specific CIN2+ rate in that stratum. To evaluate differences in CIN2+ rates between subgroups, a global Pearson chi-square test was used to compare the four regional Han groups. Prespecified two-sided Fisher’s exact tests were applied for pairwise comparisons where expected counts were low. All statistical tests were two-sided, and P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Supplementary materialThe Supplementary Material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fcimb.2026.1920297/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials
full_text_sections.results: 3.Results3.1.Cervical screening profileOverall, 12,086 women aged 20 to 65 years, with an average age of 44.83 ± 8.93 years, from four different provinces or municipalities were involved in this study (Table 1). According to information on the participants’ personal IDs, more women were born in rural areas than in urban areas. At first enrolment, the positive rate for HPV detection was 14.81%, the abnormal rate for TCTs was 7.84%, and 93 patients were diagnosed with CIN2+ and referred for further treatment (Table 2). full_text_sections.discussion: 4.Discussion4.1.Model-assisted feature importance analysisRF models were implemented to identify crucial features from the screening data and produced results that were verified by analyses of subgroups with sufficient sample sizes. As the full baseline dataset was used for model fitting without an independent test set, these results are exploratory associations rather than causal effects. The importance of feature selection has been recognised in machine learning (Parikh and Zitnick, 2010) and data mining (Visalakshi and Radha, 2014), making it a standalone research topic (Kaur et al., 2021) in machine learning. However, the application of these techniques has only recently extended to medical practice alongside artificial intelligence and has mostly involved visual recognition (Abdualgalil and Abraham, 2020). We found these techniques are particularly useful in analysing complex data with multiple categorical variables with different numbers of categories, together with age as a numerical variable, which makes them powerful tools for analysing big data, such as population data and epidemiologic data, for assisting decision making or protocol adjusting.SHAP values and permutation importance were both adopted in this study to provide perspectives with and without feature interactions. While SHAP values are obtained by considering influences between features (Lundberg and Lee, 2017), permutation importance is calculated by shuffling values of the target feature regardless of its relation to other features. Applying both methods may outline dependent and independent importance of the features, and when differences in importance are reported by the different methods, relationships between the relevant features can be analysed further. Besides, compared with permutation importance, SHAP values may provide further information on feature influence for individual samples, improving model transparency.4.2.Potential application of the age factor in cancer screeningIn this study, cervical cancer risk was associated with population features, such as region, ethnicity, urbanisation level at birth, and age, along with HPV infections and TCT results. Among these population features, some, such as region and ethnicity, displayed notable but not quantifiable associations with histopathology results, while age showed similar associations repeatedly across regions and ethnicities in this study. Furthermore, CIN2+ cases identified in participants not followed annually showed a clear bias toward older participants. However, this pattern may reflect surveillance bias and lower TCT sensitivity in older women, rather than a purely biological age effect. The biological effect of age and the surveillance-bias effect are confounded and cannot be separated in the present design. HPV prevalence has been reported for a number of regions across China by age stratum (Yan et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023), but age has rarely been analysed separately from other features or in depth. CIN2+ rates and HPV infection rates for certain populations were reported here by age stratum and showed similar intergroup profiles, but the relevant case numbers were small, limiting the reliability of these results. In addition, other researchers have reported similar HPV infection profiles but different CIN2+ profiles in other populations (Castellsagué et al., 2016; Song et al., 2020). Meanwhile, conflicting results suggesting that the importance of age is unclear have also been reported (Carozzi et al., 2014). A lack of attention to older women was noted by some researchers, but the relevant characteristics were not compared with those of other age groups to establish age-specific screening protocols (Chen et al., 2025). The main cause of the inconsistency between these profiles has not been fully identified, so further investigation is required.4.3.Test frequency and HPV infection historyAccording to local guidelines (Branch of Cancer Prevention and Control CPMA et al., 2023), persistent HPV infection was defined as testing positive for high-risk HPV in two consecutive tests at an interval of 6 to 12 months. This required a corresponding testing or screening frequency, consistent with the guideline requirements for those infected with HPV. The results of this study demonstrated a notable association between high-grade lesions and a history of high-risk HPV infection, highlighting the importance of considering repeat hrHPV positivity in screening. On the other hand, CIN2+ cases identified during the Year 3 follow-up accounted for 39.41% of the total 178 CIN2+ cases. Specifically, 20 cases (38.46% of Year 3 cases, including one cancer) were identified in women not included in annual follow-up. These 20 protocol-delayed cases, concentrated at ages 50–59, are likely attributable to surveillance bias and lower TCT sensitivity rather than age biology alone. These observations identify a surveillance limitation in the current protocol. However, earlier studies indicated that screening every 3–5 years in the general population was more economically efficient, as the benefits of shortening the screening interval to 1 year were lower than the associated increase in costs (Miller, 2003; Lees et al., 2016). Since this study did not randomise screening intervals, compare clinical strategies, or collect cost data, it cannot establish that shorter population-wide intervals are effective or cost-effective. Recommendations for screening optimisation require prospective effectiveness and health-economic evaluation. Besides, our results demonstrated insufficient willingness to undergo annual screening tests, indicating that more education and promotion regarding cervical cancer and HPV infection were required (Wang et al., 2023).4.4.HPV genotyping for additional high-risk HPV typesOur results suggested that HPV genotype was another important factor in cervical cancer risk estimation. Different cancer risks associated with HPV types other than HPV16/18 have been reported in many studies (Carozzi et al., 2014; Li et al., 2024), but guidelines for these specific HPV types have not yet been published in China. This study suggests that HPV33, 52, and 58 may be associated with a higher cervical cancer risk than other non-HPV16/18 high-risk types, and similar results have been reported by other researchers (Yan et al., 2021; Song et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023). Due to limited HPV genotyping data, only the most common high-risk types were mentioned in the results presented here, but other less common types should not be overlooked. For example, Chen et al. described the pathogenicity of HPV82 and its association with viral load (Chen et al., 2025), while the pathogenicity of HPV45 has been reported in studies conducted in other countries (Chen et al., 2014; Koestler et al., 2025). In this study, although HPV45 and HPV82 were detected in only a small number of cases, HPV82 was detected more frequently in CIN2+ cases and CIN2+ cases with repeat positivity, which agrees with the findings mentioned above. Moreover, an understanding of local HPV type distribution may enable in-depth studies of infections with multiple HPV types (Salazar et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2021) and more efficient vaccination (Jiang et al., 2019). Routine implementation of extended genotyping requires confirmation in uniformly tested populations to fully validate its clinical utility and cost-effectiveness.4.5.Limitations and future requirementsThis study has several limitations. First, extended HPV genotyping was not uniformly performed for all participants. This site- and screening-round dependence can introduce selection bias and prevent population-wide inference. Second, routine HPV retesting was not conducted in Years 1 and 2 of the screening protocol, limiting the ability to assess type-specific persistence of HPV infections. full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionIn this research, rates of high-grade CIN and high-risk HPV infection were analysed across different regions, ethnicities, and age strata. Based on exploratory RF/SHAP modelling, our results suggested an association between age and the CIN2+ rate, and age, HPV16, and TCT were prominent exploratory predictors. Directly standardised comparisons did not support greater susceptibility by region, birthplace, or ethnicity, and genotype findings arose from incomplete site-dependent testing. However, given the limitations outlined above—including non-uniform extended genotyping, absence of confounder data, and sparse CIN2+ outcomes—these findings are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted with caution. Moreover, our preliminary observations from the subset with extended genotyping suggest that HPV33, 52, and 58 may pose higher risks than other non-HPV16/18 types. But these findings require confirmation in future studies with uniform extended genotyping across all participants to fully validate their significance. Finally, while HPV genotyping and repeat positivity show potential for cancer risk estimation, independent validation, uniform genotyping, prespecified multivariable analysis, and health-economic evaluation are required before screening-interval or policy changes can be recommended.

The common cervical cancer prevention approach implemented by China is screening with cytology inspection, HPV testing, and colposcopy-guided biopsy (Molina et al., 2024). However, due to complicated conditions across the country, screening protocols and coverage vary in different regions, and a more effective and adaptable protocol is required (Jinghe and Qiang, 2022).Efforts were made to collect data worldwide to optimise resources and strategies for regional cervical cancer screening. papers.title_original: A multi-centre study on cervical cancer screening reveals population-related impact on cervical intraepithelial neoplasia rate

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the impact of cervical cancer screening on the population-related rates of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade 2 or worse (CIN2+), addressing the need to understand how screening programs affect disease prevalence across different demographic and geographic groups.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a multi-centre, operational study conducted in four provinces (Sichuan, Zhejiang, Inner Mongolia, and Beijing) involving 12,086 women aged 20 to 65 with a history of sexual activity. Participants were recruited for cervical cancer screening, with specific exclusion criteria including prior cervical cancer diagnosis, current chemotherapy or radiotherapy, pregnancy, and HPV vaccination history.
analysis.methods: Cervical exfoliated cells were collected and preserved for TCT and HPV genotyping. HPV DNA was detected using PCR-fluorescence probing, and extended genotyping was performed for participants in Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia. A 10-fold cross-validation was used to assess the model's ability to capture relations between features and CIN2+ results, and feature importance was evaluated using permutation-induced changes in prediction accuracy and SHAP values.
analysis.main_results: At first enrolment, the HPV detection rate was 14.81%, and the abnormal TCT rate was 7.84%. A total of 93 patients were diagnosed with CIN2+ and referred for further treatment. The overall cumulative three-year CIN2+ rate was 1.47% (178/12,086), while the baseline rate was 0.77% (93/12,086). Crude CIN2+ rates varied between regions, with the lowest in Zhejiang (0.43%) and the highest in Inner Mongolia (0.93%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that while some numerical variations in crude CIN2+ rates were observed across subgroups, these differences did not reach statistical significance in the cohort. This study provides novel insights into the population-related impact of cervical cancer screening on CIN2+ rates, highlighting the importance of demographic and geographic factors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform cervical cancer screening programs by highlighting the need to consider demographic and geographic variations in CIN2+ rates, potentially guiding targeted interventions and resource allocation in high-risk regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was an operational, site- and round-dependent implementation rather than a random sample, and the number of positive cases at the first screen was insufficient for robust statistical analyses on certain features. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This multi-centre study investigated the impact of cervical cancer screening on cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) rates across different demographic and geographic groups. The study included 12,086 women aged 20 to 65 with a history of sexual activity, recruited from four provinces in China. HPV detection and TCT were performed, with extended genotyping available in some regions. The overall cumulative three-year CIN2+ rate was 1.47%, while the baseline rate was 0.77%. Crude CIN2+ rates varied between regions, with the lowest in Zhejiang and the highest in Inner Mongolia. However, statistical tests showed no significant differences across subgroups. The study's findings suggest that while demographic and geographic factors may influence CIN2+ rates, further research is needed to validate these observations. The evidence is moderate due to the study's operational design and limited sample size for certain analyses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查 宫颈癌 筛查对宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN) 2 级或更严重 (CIN2+) 的人群相关率的影响,解决了解筛查计划如何影响不同人口和地理群体的疾病 患病率 的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项在四个省(四川、浙江、内蒙古和北京)开展的多中心、操作性研究,涉及 12,086 名年龄在 20 岁至 65 岁之间有性活动史的女性。招募参与者进行 宫颈癌 筛查,具体排除标准包括既往 宫颈癌、诊断、当前化疗或放疗、妊娠和 HPV 疫苗接种 病史。
elements_zh.methods: 收集并保存宫颈脱落细胞用于 TCT 和 HPV 基因分型。使用 PCR 荧光探针检测 HPV DNA,并对四川、北京和内蒙古的参与者进行了扩展基因分型。使用 10 倍交叉验证来评估模型捕获特征和 CIN2+ 结果之间关系的能力,并使用排列引起的预测精度和 SHAP 值的变化来评估特征重要性。
elements_zh.main_results: 首次入组时HPV检出率为14.81%,TCT异常率为7.84%。共有 93 名患者被诊断为 CIN2+,并转诊进一步接受 治疗。总体累计三年 CIN2+ 率为 1.47% (178/12,086),而基线率为 0.77% (93/12,086)。粗CIN2+比率因地区而异,浙江最低(0.43%),内蒙古最高(0.93%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,虽然在各个亚组中观察到粗 CIN2+ 率存在一些数值差异,但这些差异在 队列研究 中并未达到统计显着性。这项研究为 宫颈癌 筛查对 CIN2+ 率与人群相关的影响提供了新颖的见解,强调了人口和地理因素的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为 宫颈癌 筛查计划提供信息,强调需要考虑 CIN2+ 发生率的人口和地理差异,并有可能指导高风险地区的针对性干预措施和资源分配。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项可操作的、与地点和回合相关的实施,而不是随机样本,并且第一次筛选的阳性病例数量不足以对某些特征进行稳健的统计分析。由于这些限制,证据是中等的。

papers.title: Oral epithelial dysplasia, role of histopathological diagnosis and human papillomavirus infection
papers.abstract: Oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) is regarded as the main histopathological precursor to oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Histopathological grading of dysplasia remains the cornerstone of OED assessment and yet, its predictive value is limited. In addition to histopathological diagnosis of OED, other histopathological diagnosis can simultaneously occur in a lesion. The World Health Organization (WHO) recognized another distinct entity of OED year 2017: human papillomavirus (HPV) associated OED. The aim of this dissertation study was to evaluate three factors in OED that could influence the malignant transformation: classification of OED, additional histopathological diagnoses to OED and HPV infection. All OED patients from the Department of Oral Pathology and Radiology, Institute of Dentistry, University of Turku, Turku, Finland between the years 1982 and 2011 were retrospectively retrieved from the oral pathology registry. Patients who developed OSCC were identified from the Finnish Cancer Registry by their Finnish social security number. ICD codes C00 and C02 – C06 were considered as OSCC. First, three-tier grading was used representing the real-life situation. Then the effect of additional histopathological diagnosis to malignant transformation was evaluated. Later, re-evaluation of OEDs with two-tier grading was performed to investigate if it has more objectivity and therefore could better predict OSCC development. To investigate the role of HPV detection in OED and its progress, HPV was detected on protein level (p16), HPV DNA level (polymerase chain reaction, PCR) and the presence of high-risk HPV mRNA (in situ hybridization, ISH). There were 922 patients with OED in the oral pathology registry. Their mean age was 60 years and 69% were women. The most common location for OED lesion was mobile tongue. There were found 63.7% mild, 29.5% moderate and severe 3.4% of the OEDs cases, and the rest OEDs were not graded. After the re-evaluation into two-tier grading, 84.1% were low-grade dysplasia and 15.9% high-grade dysplasia. The mean follow-up time of OEDs was 5.9 years (range 0.7-29.0, SD=5.9). Of OED patients, 7.8% progressed to OSCC. Of the additional diagnoses, hyperkeratosis, hyperplasia, and ulcer were the most common findings, found in 44.9%, 27.3% and 18.1% of the samples, respectively. Positivity for HPV with the three laboratory methods varied between 0.9-5.9%. With statistical analysis, only location on the mobile tongue (Fisher’s exact test, p=0.016) and the severity of OED were associated with the risk of OSCC development (Hazard ratio, HR=3.44, 95% confidence interval, CI 0.83-14.19). The more severe grade of OED had the shorter time for OSCC development (Jonkcheere Terpstra -test p=0.025). Malignant transformation was not associated with any of the three laboratory detection methods of HPV (p16 p=0.2, PCR p=0.7, and mRNA ISH p=0.7) individually or combined. Only two factors with OED had predictive value of malignant transformation: location of OED on the mobile tongue and the more severe histopathological grade of OED. Our findings support the concept that the carcinogenesis of OED is uncertain. HPV-infection was unreliably detected and did not change the risk for malignant transformation. Alternative biomarkers than histopathological picture and HPV detection are needed for the OED risk assessment.

papers.title: Methodological drivers, reporting completeness, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations: A scoping review
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is widely reported as cost-effective, but reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) are shaped by model structure, assumptions, comparator choice, vaccine price, threshold selection, and local screening context. Previous reviews have summarized cost-effectiveness findings but have less often examined why conclusions differ across settings. OBJECTIVE: To map methodological evolution, drivers of variation, reporting completeness, methodological credibility, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted using the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley, refined by Levac et al., and informed by JBI guidance for scoping reviews. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR, and the protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025, with a final search conducted on January 2, 2026. Forty-four records were mapped. Thirty-three full comparative economic evaluations formed the primary synthesis; 11 partial or non-standard economic evidence records were retained as contextual evidence. The Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) checklist was applied retrospectively to assess reporting completeness, and a descriptive structured appraisal was used to examine methodological credibility across six health-economic domains. A Welte-informed assessment was used to examine target-context contextualization. RESULTS: The evidence base evolved from early static cohort models to dynamic transmission and individual-based approaches, while static models remained common in LMIC-focused standardized-tool analyses. The main drivers of variation were vaccine price, discounting, herd-immunity assumptions, cross-protection assumptions, and threshold selection. Reporting completeness varied and did not necessarily correspond to methodological credibility. Relevance to a study's own decision setting did not imply that its ICER could be transferred to other countries. Eleven contextual records showed emerging policy questions around delivery costs, fiscal consequences, uptake, risk-benefit framing, and non-ICER-based decision support. CONCLUSION: The economic value reported for HPV vaccination depends on the assumptions, comparators, vaccine prices, thresholds, and local screening contexts used in each evaluation rather than on the vaccine alone. Future evaluations should explicitly justify the choice of comparator, model structure, vaccine-price assumptions, discount rates, thresholds, uncertainty analysis, and transferability assumptions. Although formal cost-effectiveness analyses of single-dose HPV vaccination have begun to emerge, evidence remains limited, particularly regarding durability, waning, delivery feasibility, gender-neutral vaccination in LMICs, and country-specific evaluations in underrepresented regions.

papers.title_zh: HPV 疫苗接种 经济评估中的方法驱动因素、报告完整性和可转移性:范围界定审查
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is widely reported as cost-effective, but reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) are shaped by model structure, assumptions, comparator choice, vaccine price, threshold selection, and local screening context. Previous reviews have summarized cost-effectiveness findings but have less often examined why conclusions differ across settings. OBJECTIVE: To map methodological evolution, drivers of variation, reporting completeness, methodological credibility, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted using the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley, refined by Levac et al., and informed by JBI guidance for scoping reviews. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR, and the protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025, with a final search conducted on January 2, 2026. Forty-four records were mapped. Thirty-three full comparative economic evaluations formed the primary synthesis; 11 partial or non-standard economic evidence records were retained as contextual evidence. The Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) checklist was applied retrospectively to assess reporting completeness, and a descriptive structured appraisal was used to examine methodological credibility across six health-economic domains. A Welte-informed assessment was used to examine target-context contextualization. RESULTS: The evidence base evolved from early static cohort models to dynamic transmission and individual-based approaches, while static models remained common in LMIC-focused standardized-tool analyses. The main drivers of variation were vaccine price, discounting, herd-immunity assumptions, cross-protection assumptions, and threshold selection. Reporting completeness varied and did not necessarily correspond to methodological credibility. Relevance to a study's own decision setting did not imply that its ICER could be transferred to other countries. Eleven contextual records showed emerging policy questions around delivery costs, fiscal consequences, uptake, risk-benefit framing, and non-ICER-based decision support. CONCLUSION: The economic value reported for HPV vaccination depends on the assumptions, comparators, vaccine prices, thresholds, and local screening contexts used in each evaluation rather than on the vaccine alone. Future evaluations should explicitly justify the choice of comparator, model structure, vaccine-price assumptions, discount rates, thresholds, uncertainty analysis, and transferability assumptions. Although formal cost-effectiveness analyses of single-dose HPV vaccination have begun to emerge, evidence remains limited, particularly regarding durability, waning, delivery feasibility, gender-neutral vaccination in LMICs, and country-specific evaluations in underrepresented regions.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 被广泛报道为具有成本效益,但报告的增量成本效益比 (ICER) 是由模型结构、假设、比较器选择、疫苗 价格、阈值选择和本地筛选环境决定的。之前的评论总结了成本效益的研究结果,但很少研究为什么结论在不同环境下会有所不同。目的:绘制 HPV 进化 经济评估中的方法论 进化、变异驱动因素、报告完整性、方法论可信度和可转移性。方法:使用 Arksey 和 O'Malley 提出的方法框架进行范围界定审查,并由 Levac 等人完善,并参考 JBI 范围界定指南。报告遵循 PRISMA-ScR,并且该协议已在开放科学框架 (OSF) 上预先注册。PubMed、Scopus、PsycINFO、Embase、Web of Science 和 CINAHL 的检索时间为 2003 年 1 月 1 日至 2025 年 12 月 31 日,最终检索于 2026 年 1 月 2 日进行。映射了 44 条记录。三十三个完整的比较经济评价形成了初步综合;11 条部分或非标准经济证据记录被保留作为背景证据。回顾性地应用了 2022 年综合卫生经济评估报告标准 (CHEERS 2022) 清单来评估报告的完整性,并使用描述性结构化评估来检查六个卫生经济领域的方法学可信度。使用 Welte 知情评估来检查目标情境情境化。结果:证据基础从早期静态 队列研究 模型发展到动态 传播 和基于个体的方法,而静态模型在以中低收入国家为重点的标准化工具分析中仍然很常见。变化的主要驱动因素是 疫苗 价格、折扣、群体免疫假设、交叉保护假设和阈值选择。报告的完整性各不相同,并不一定符合方法论的可信度。与研究自身决策制定的相关性并不意味着其 ICER 可以转移到其他国家。十一项背景记录显示了围绕交付成本、财政后果、吸收、风险收益框架和非基于 ICER 的决策支持的新政策问题。结论:HPV 疫苗接种 报告的经济价值取决于每次评估中使用的假设、比较器、疫苗 价格、阈值和当地筛查环境,而不是仅取决于 疫苗。未来的评估应明确证明比较器、模型结构、疫苗价格假设、贴现率、阈值、不确定性分析和可转移性假设的选择的合理性。尽管单剂 HPV 疫苗接种 的正式成本效益分析已经开始出现,但证据仍然有限,特别是在耐久性、衰退、交付可行性、中低收入国家中性别中立的 疫苗接种 以及代表性不足地区的具体国家评估方面。

papers.title: Neurological Complications of Oncogenic Viruses: Mechanisms, Clinical Manifestations, and Emerging Insights.
papers.abstract: Oncogenic viruses are widely recognized for their pivotal role in malignant transformation; however, their capacity to induce neurological disorders has received comparatively less attention. Increasing evidence indicates that several oncogenic viruses, including human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), are associated with a broad spectrum of neurological complications involving both the central and peripheral nervous systems. These manifestations arise through diverse mechanisms, including direct viral neuroinvasion, persistent infection, immune-mediated tissue injury, chronic neuroinflammation, and disruption of neurovascular integrity. Moreover, virus-induced molecular alterations, such as oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic remodelling, and aberrant cytokine signalling, contribute t neuronal dysfunction and disease progression. In this review, we critically examine the current understanding of the neurological complications associated with major oncogenic viruses by integrating evidence from molecular, experimental, and clinical studies. We first discuss the general mechanisms by which viral infections induce neurological injury, highlighting pathways shared among neurotropic and non-neurotropic viruses. We then summarise the neurological manifestations and virus-specific pathogenic mechanisms associated with each oncogenic virus, emphasising both common and distinct molecular pathways underlying neuropathogenesis. Finally, we address current diagnostic challenges, emerging biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies while identifying critical knowledge gaps that limit causal interpretation and clinical translation. A comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions between oncogenic viruses, the immune system, and the nervous system will facilitate earlier diagnosis, improve patient management, and support the development of targeted therapeutic approaches for virus-associated neurological disorders.

papers.title_zh: 致癌病毒的神经并发症:机制、临床表现和新见解。
papers.source_body_en: Oncogenic viruses are widely recognized for their pivotal role in malignant transformation; however, their capacity to induce neurological disorders has received comparatively less attention. Increasing evidence indicates that several oncogenic viruses, including human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), are associated with a broad spectrum of neurological complications involving both the central and peripheral nervous systems. These manifestations arise through diverse mechanisms, including direct viral neuroinvasion, persistent infection, immune-mediated tissue injury, chronic neuroinflammation, and disruption of neurovascular integrity. Moreover, virus-induced molecular alterations, such as oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic remodelling, and aberrant cytokine signalling, contribute t neuronal dysfunction and disease progression. In this review, we critically examine the current understanding of the neurological complications associated with major oncogenic viruses by integrating evidence from molecular, experimental, and clinical studies. We first discuss the general mechanisms by which viral infections induce neurological injury, highlighting pathways shared among neurotropic and non-neurotropic viruses. We then summarise the neurological manifestations and virus-specific pathogenic mechanisms associated with each oncogenic virus, emphasising both common and distinct molecular pathways underlying neuropathogenesis. Finally, we address current diagnostic challenges, emerging biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies while identifying critical knowledge gaps that limit causal interpretation and clinical translation. A comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions between oncogenic viruses, the immune system, and the nervous system will facilitate earlier diagnosis, improve patient management, and support the development of targeted therapeutic approaches for virus-associated neurological disorders.
papers.abstract_zh: 致癌病毒因其在恶性转化中的关键作用而被广泛认可。然而,它们引起神经系统疾病的能力相对较少受到关注。越来越多的证据表明,多种致癌病毒,包括人类 T 细胞白血病病毒 1 型 (HTLV-1)、人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)、乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV)、丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 和卡波西肉瘤相关疱疹病毒 (KSHV),与涉及中枢和周围神经系统的广泛神经系统并发症有关。这些表现是通过多种机制产生的,包括直接病毒神经侵袭、持续感染、免疫介导的组织损伤、慢性神经炎症和神经血管完整性破坏。此外,病毒诱导的分子改变,如氧化应激、线粒体功能障碍、表观遗传重塑和异常的细胞因子信号传导,会导致神经元功能障碍和疾病进展。在这篇综述中,我们通过整合分子、实验和临床研究的证据,批判性地研究了目前对与主要致癌病毒相关的神经并发症的理解。我们首先讨论病毒感染引起神经损伤的一般机制,强调嗜神经病毒和非嗜神经病毒之间共享的途径。然后,我们总结了与每种致癌病毒相关的神经学表现和病毒特异性致病机制,强调神经发病机制中常见和独特的分子途径。最后,我们解决当前的诊断挑战、新兴生物标志物和治疗策略,同时确定限制因果解释和临床转化的关键知识差距。全面了解致癌病毒、免疫系统和神经系统之间复杂的相互作用将有助于早期 诊断,改善患者管理,并支持开发针对病毒相关神经系统疾病的靶向治疗方法。

papers.title: HPV vaccination coverage and barriers for people with disability: A scoping review
papers.abstract: This scoping review explored human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage and barriers for people with disability. Our global search identified 33 studies, all from high-income countries, published between 2006 and 2025. We found evidence of inequalities in HPV vaccination coverage for people with disability across a range of countries, sexes/genders, settings, and disability groups. Common vaccination barriers included misassumptions around sexual activity, lack of vaccination recommendations from healthcare professionals in primarily healthcare-facility-based HPV vaccination programme settings, and lack of staff training/resources. There were marked gaps in population-wide research for all people with disability, research from low- and middle-income settings, and research including deaf or blind communities, or people with physical or psychosocial disability. Disability-inclusive research methodologies were limited and should be prioritized to ensure future research meets community needs. If HPV vaccination targets are to be achieved, equitable access must be supported for all people, including people with disability.

If HPV vaccination targets are to be achieved, equitable access must be supported for all people, including people with disability.

papers.title: Spotlights on cervical cancer: progression, diagnosis and clinical manifestations, epidemiology, treatment approaches, role of artificial intelligence and future directions.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer remains a major cause of illness and death among women worldwide, especially in low- and middle-income countries, where access to vaccination, screening, and advanced treatment is limited. SIGNIFICANCE: This review offers a comprehensive overview of the current evidence on cervical cancer, covering its epidemiology, molecular progression, clinical manifestations, diagnostic strategies, and emerging therapeutic approaches. It also emphasizes the integration of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, into cervical cancer screening, diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and treatment planning. In addition, it highlights recent advances in precision medicine, liquid biopsy, targeted therapies, immunotherapy, and nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems, while identifying current challenges and future research priorities. KEY FINDINGS: This review article pointed out the recent applied technologies for early diagnosis of cervical cancer e.g. biosensors which can overcome the limitations of immunohistochemistry and biochemical based assays. Therapeutic vaccines have also been developed as an alternative to therapeutic drugs and surgical operations for the prevention of cervical cancer. In addition, targeted delivery and nanotechnology applications in tumor diagnosis, investigation, and management as well as the delivery of HPV vaccines. Artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated considerable potential for the early detection of HPV infections and management of cervical cancer through surgical planning via AI-enhanced robotic systems. CONCLUSIONS: Cervical cancer research should focus on precision medicine, integrating recent models of artificial intelligence, advanced screening technologies, immunotherapy, and global public health initiatives. Combining these approaches could lead to improving early tumor detection, optimizing treatment outcomes, reducing disease burden, and contributing to eliminating cervical cancer.

papers.title: Kinesin superfamily proteins in head and neck cancer: Mechanisms, clinical implications, and therapeutic potential.
papers.abstract: Head and neck cancer, particularly head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), remains a substantial cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality. Although surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy have improved disease management, the prognosis of patients with advanced or recurrent disease remains poor. Increasing evidence suggests that kinesin superfamily proteins (KIFs), microtubule-based molecular motors involved in intracellular transport and chromosome dynamics, have important roles in head and neck cancer. This review examines the current evidence on KIF dysregulation in head and neck cancer, with particular emphasis on their contributions to tumor biology, regulatory mechanisms, clinical relevance, and therapeutic potential. This narrative review examined peer-reviewed preclinical and clinical studies on KIF involvement in major features of head and neck cancer, including cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), cancer stemness, cell-cycle progression, apoptosis, and treatment resistance. We also considered evidence on regulatory mechanisms, including non-coding RNAs, ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis, and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification, along with studies investigating KIFs as prognostic biomarkers or therapeutic targets. The available evidence supports an important role for several KIFs in head and neck cancer progression, particularly through effects on cell-cycle regulation, survival, migration, and oncogenic signaling. Nevertheless, KIF activity is not uniformly oncogenic. The effects of individual family members appear to depend on tumor subtype, anatomical site, molecular context, and human papillomavirus (HPV) status. In addition, the predominance of experimental studies and relatively small clinical cohorts limits the strength of current clinical evidence. Future studies should clarify the context-specific functions of individual KIFs using HPV- and subtype-stratified models and integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and epigenetic approaches. Validation in clinically relevant models and larger, independent patient cohorts will be important for establishing their biomarker value. Selective kinesin inhibitors also warrant further investigation to determine whether these proteins can be effectively exploited for therapeutic intervention in head and neck cancer.

This review examines the current evidence on KIF dysregulation in head and neck cancer, with particular emphasis on their contributions to tumor biology, regulatory mechanisms, clinical relevance, and therapeutic potential. This narrative review examined peer-reviewed preclinical and clinical studies on KIF involvement in major features of head and neck cancer, including cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), cancer stemness, cell-cycle progression, apoptosis, and treatment resistance. We also considered evidence on regulatory mechanisms, including non-coding RNAs, ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis, and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification, along with studies investigating KIFs as prognostic biomarkers or therapeutic targets. The effects of individual family members appear to depend on tumor subtype, anatomical site, molecular context, and human papillomavirus (HPV) status. In addition, the predominance of experimental studies and relatively small clinical cohorts limits the strength of current clinical evidence. Future studies should clarify the context-specific functions of individual KIFs using HPV- and subtype-stratified models and integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and epigenetic approaches. Validation in clinically relevant models and larger, independent patient cohorts will be important for establishing their biomarker value. Selective kinesin inhibitors also warrant further investigation to determine whether these proteins can be effectively exploited for therapeutic intervention in head and neck cancer.

papers.abstract_zh: 头颈癌,特别是头颈鳞状细胞癌 (HNSCC),仍然是癌症相关发病率和 死亡率 的重要原因。尽管手术、放疗、化疗、靶向治疗和免疫治疗改善了疾病管理,但晚期或复发性疾病患者的预后仍然较差。越来越多的证据表明,驱动蛋白超家族蛋白(KIF)是一种基于微管的分子马达,参与​​细胞内运输和染色体动力学,在头颈癌中发挥着重要作用。本综述探讨了头颈癌中 KIF 失调的当前证据,特别强调其对肿瘤生物学、调节机制、临床相关性和治疗潜力的贡献。这篇叙述性综述审查了同行评审的 KIF 参与头颈癌主要特征的临床前和临床研究,包括细胞增殖、侵袭、转移、上皮间质转化 (EMT)、癌症干性、细胞周期进展、细胞凋亡和 治疗 耐药。我们还考虑了调节机制的证据,包括非编码 RNA、泛素介导的蛋白水解和 N6-甲基腺苷 (m6A) 修饰,以及调查 KIF 作为预后生物标志物或治疗靶点的研究。现有证据支持多种 KIF 在头颈癌进展中发挥重要作用,特别是通过对细胞周期调节、存活、迁移和致癌信号传导的影响。然而,KIF 活性并不均具有致癌性。个体家庭成员的影响似乎取决于肿瘤亚型、解剖部位、分子背景和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 状态。此外,实验研究的主导地位和相对较小的临床 队列研究 限制了当前临床证据的强度。未来的研究应使用 HPV 和亚型分层模型以及整合的转录组学、蛋白质组学和表观遗传学方法来阐明各个 KIF 的特定功能。临床相关模型和更大的独立患者 队列研究 的验证对于确定其生物标志物价值非常重要。选择性驱动蛋白抑制剂也值得进一步研究,以确定这些蛋白质是否可以有效地用于头颈癌的治疗干预。

papers.title: Advances in neoadjuvant therapy for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (Review).
papers.abstract: The majority of head and neck cancers arise from the mucosal squamous epithelium of the oral cavity, pharynx and larynx, and are collectively referred to as head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). A multimodal standard of care is applied for case management. Primary oral cavity cancers are treated with resection followed by adjuvant cisplatin‐based chemoradiotherapy (CRT), and definitive concurrent CRT is applied for pharyngeal or laryngeal disease. In human papillomavirus‐negative patients who are medically unfit for platinum treatment, the epidermal growth factor receptor‐directed monoclonal antibody cetuximab is administered concomitantly with radiotherapy (RT). More recently, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have redefined systemic therapy for recurrent/metastatic HNSCC, yielding durable responses and a survival benefit. In total, 65‐70% of patients present with stage III‐IVA locally advanced (LA) disease, a scenario associated with therapeutic challenges and a marked deterioration in the quality of life. Neoadjuvant therapy is designed to downstage the primary tumor, eradicate occult micrometastatic disease and enhance locoregional control before definitive surgery or RT, thus offering a rational strategy for organ preservation. Contemporary regimens integrate taxane, platinum and 5‐fluorouracil induction chemotherapy with RT, and early‐phase trials have explored the feasibility and efficacy of incorporating ICIs into neoadjuvant protocols. The present review summarizes the evolution of neoadjuvant therapy for LA HNSCC, with particular emphasis on emerging immunotherapy‐based paradigms and their potential to improve oncological and functional outcomes.

papers.abstract_zh: 大多数头颈癌起源于口腔、咽和喉部的粘膜鳞状上皮,统称为头颈鳞状细胞癌(HNSCC)。病例管理采用多模式护理标准。原发性口腔癌的治疗方法是切除,然后进行基于顺铂的辅助放化疗 (CRT),并且针对咽或喉部疾病应用明确的同步 CRT。在医学上不适合铂类药物 人乳头瘤病毒 的 人乳头瘤病毒 阴性患者中,表皮生长因子受体导向的单克隆抗体西妥昔单抗与放疗 (RT) 同时给药。最近,免疫检查点抑制剂 (ICIs) 重新定义了复发/转移性 HNSCC 的全身治疗,产生持久的反应和生存获益。总的来说,65-70% 的患者患有 III-IVA 期局部晚期 (LA) 疾病,这种情况与治疗挑战和生活质量显着恶化相关。新辅助治疗旨在降低原发肿瘤的阶段,根除隐匿性微转移性疾病,并在确定性手术或放疗前增强局部控制,从而为器官保存提供合理的策略。当代治疗方案将紫杉烷、铂类和 5-氟尿嘧啶诱导化疗与放疗相结合,早期试验已经探索了将 ICI 纳入新辅助治疗方案的可行性和有效性。本综述总结了 LA HNSCC 新辅助治疗的 进化,特别强调新兴的基于免疫治疗的范例及其改善肿瘤和功能结果的潜力。

papers.title: Social Media and HPV Vaccine Hesitancy: How Misinformation Affects Latino Parents
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine coverage in the United States remains suboptimal, with Latino communities facing disproportionately lower rates and a higher burden of HPV-associated cancers. Health misinformation and disinformation (M&D) on social media represents a barrier to HPV vaccine uptake, yet little empirical evidence exists on how such content shapes vaccine decision-making. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 98 Latino parents drawn from two randomized, community-based prospective trials conducted across four U.S. Eligible participants confirmed their HPV vaccine-eligible child remained unvaccinated and reported active social media use. A structured survey assessed platform use, access frequency, health information-seeking behaviors, and exposure to HPV vaccine-specific social media content. All 98 parents reported regular social media use. Facebook (68%), Instagram (61%), WhatsApp (61%), and YouTube (48%) were the most used platforms. Three-quarters of parents (77%, n = 75) reported vaccine-related social media exposure in the prior year, with 99% (n = 74) characterizing it as negative. Over half (52%, n = 51) recalled HPV vaccine-specific content, all of whom described it as negative. 41% of all parents (n = 40) reported that perceived negative social media content directly influenced their decision to delay or refuse HPV vaccination; this proportion rose to 78% among those with HPV-specific negative exposure. Social media M&D is a self-reported, substantial driver of HPV vaccine hesitancy among Latino parents. Passive exposure and negativity of vaccine content encountered underscore an urgent need for culturally tailored counter-messaging strategies that operate within social media platforms.

papers.title_zh: 社交媒体和 HPV 疫苗 犹豫不决:错误信息如何影响拉丁裔父母
papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine coverage in the United States remains suboptimal, with Latino communities facing disproportionately lower rates and a higher burden of HPV-associated cancers. Health misinformation and disinformation (M&D) on social media represents a barrier to HPV vaccine uptake, yet little empirical evidence exists on how such content shapes vaccine decision-making. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 98 Latino parents drawn from two randomized, community-based prospective trials conducted across four U.S. Eligible participants confirmed their HPV vaccine-eligible child remained unvaccinated and reported active social media use. A structured survey assessed platform use, access frequency, health information-seeking behaviors, and exposure to HPV vaccine-specific social media content. All 98 parents reported regular social media use. Facebook (68%), Instagram (61%), WhatsApp (61%), and YouTube (48%) were the most used platforms. Three-quarters of parents (77%, n = 75) reported vaccine-related social media exposure in the prior year, with 99% (n = 74) characterizing it as negative. Over half (52%, n = 51) recalled HPV vaccine-specific content, all of whom described it as negative. 41% of all parents (n = 40) reported that perceived negative social media content directly influenced their decision to delay or refuse HPV vaccination; this proportion rose to 78% among those with HPV-specific negative exposure. Social media M&D is a self-reported, substantial driver of HPV vaccine hesitancy among Latino parents. Passive exposure and negativity of vaccine content encountered underscore an urgent need for culturally tailored counter-messaging strategies that operate within social media platforms.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 在美国的覆盖率仍然不理想,拉丁裔社区面临着 HPV 相关癌症的不成比例的较低发病率和较高负担。社交媒体上的健康错误信息和虚假信息 (M&D) 是 HPV 疫苗 吸收的障碍,但很少有经验证据表明此类内容如何影响 疫苗 决策。我们对 98 名拉丁裔父母进行了一项横断面研究,这些父母来自两项随机、基于社区的前瞻性试验,这些试验在四名符合条件的美国参与者中进行,证实他们符合 HPV 疫苗 条件的孩子仍未接种疫苗,并报告了活跃的社交媒体使用情况。一项结构化调查评估了平台使用情况、访问频率、健康信息寻求行为以及 HPV 疫苗 特定社交媒体内容的暴露情况。所有 98 名家长均表示经常使用社交媒体。Facebook (68%)、Instagram (61%)、WhatsApp (61%) 和 YouTube (48%) 是最常用的平台。四分之三的家长 (77%,n = 75) 报告称,去年曾在社交媒体上曝光过与 疫苗 相关的内容,其中 99% (n = 74) 将其描述为负面。超过一半 (52%,n = 51) 的人回忆起 HPV 疫苗 的特定内容,所有这些人都将其描述为阴性。41% 的家长 (n = 40) 表示,感知到的负面社交媒体内容直接影响了他们推迟或拒绝 HPV 疫苗接种 的决定;在 HPV 特异性阴性暴露人群中,这一比例上升至 78%。据自我报告,社交媒体 M&D 是拉丁裔父母对 HPV 疫苗 犹豫不决的重要驱动因素。所遇到的 疫苗 内容的被动曝光和负面性凸显了迫切需要在社交媒体平台上运作的、根据文化量身定制的反信息策略。

papers.title: HPV ‐Positive Keratinizing Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Is Associated With Better Survival: A NCDB Study
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prognostic relevance of human papillomavirus (HPV) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: The National Cancer Data Base (NCDB) was used to query patients with NPC and available HPV testing data between 2010 and 2017. Logistic regression was performed to predict factors associated with HPV testing and HPV positivity. Overall survival (OS) was evaluated using Kaplan Meier analysis between HPV-positive versus HPV-negative cohorts. Univariate and multivariate analyses using Cox proportional hazards modeling were performed to assess for factors associated with OS. RESULTS: Among our cohort of 5081 patients, 3177 (62.5%) underwent HPV testing. Kaplan Meier analysis revealed improved OS among HPV-positive patients with keratinizing subtype of NPC (log rank p < 0.001). No differences in OS were observed in patients with other histologic subtypes of NPC. On multivariate analysis of the keratinizing SCC cohort, HPV positivity was associated better OS after controlling for sex, age, race, insurance status, facility volume, facility type, zip code level education, Charlson comorbidity score, staging, and treatment (HR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.70-0.94, p = 0.006). CONCLUSION: HPV status was independently associated with improved OS among patients with keratinizing subtype of NPC. Incorporation of HPV testing may be warranted in the workup of NPC.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the prognostic relevance of human papillomavirus (HPV) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). The authors sought to address a knowledge gap regarding the impact of HPV on survival outcomes in NPC patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis using the National Cancer Data Base (NCDB) was conducted on patients with NPC and available HPV testing data between 2010 and 2017. The study included 5081 patients, of whom 3177 (62.5%) underwent HPV testing.
analysis.methods: Logistic regression was used to predict factors associated with HPV testing, and Kaplan Meier analysis was performed to evaluate overall survival (OS) between HPV-positive and HPV-negative cohorts. Cox proportional hazards modeling was applied for multivariate analysis of factors influencing OS.
analysis.main_results: Kaplan Meier analysis revealed improved overall survival (OS) among HPV-positive patients with keratinizing subtype of NPC (log rank p < 0.001). On multivariate analysis of the keratinizing SCC cohort, HPV positivity was associated with better OS after controlling for various factors (HR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.70-0.94, p = 0.006).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HPV status was independently associated with improved OS among patients with keratinizing subtype of NPC, highlighting a novel association between HPV and survival outcomes in this specific histologic subgroup.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the need for HPV testing in the workup of NPC, particularly for patients with keratinizing subtypes, to guide prognosis and treatment decisions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on existing data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prognostic relevance of human papillomavirus (HPV) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) using the National Cancer Data Base (NCDB). It found that HPV positivity was associated with improved overall survival (OS) in patients with keratinizing subtype NPC, after adjusting for multiple factors. The results suggest that HPV status may be an independent predictor of survival in this specific subgroup, potentially influencing clinical decision-making. However, the study's retrospective design and reliance on existing data limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

papers.title: HPV Knowledge, Vaccination Uptake, and Barriers to Vaccination among Healthcare Workers at a University Hospital in Türkiye: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Healthcare workers play a central role in human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination counselling and substantially influence vaccine acceptance. However, adequate theoretical knowledge does not necessarily translate into personal vaccination uptake or effective preventive behaviors. Objective This study aimed to assess HPV-related knowledge, personal HPV vaccination uptake, self-reported barriers to vaccination, and factors independently associated with HPV knowledge among healthcare workers at a university hospital in Türkiye. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at Süleyman Demirel University Research and Application Hospital between 15 December 2025 and 15 February 2026. A total of 288 healthcare workers participated in the study. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire and a 33-item Turkish HPV Knowledge Scale. Group differences were evaluated using Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests, followed by Dwass–Steel–Critchlow–Fligner post-hoc comparisons where appropriate. Effect sizes were reported as r and epsilon squared (ε2). Factors independently associated with total HPV knowledge scores were examined using multivariable linear regression with HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. Results The mean age of the participants was 36.38 ± 8.62 years, 70.1% were female, and 45.5% were physicians. The mean total HPV Knowledge Scale score was 24.62 ± 6.11 (out of 33). Knowledge gaps were particularly evident regarding vaccine availability and access, age-related indications, and male vaccination. Total knowledge scores differed significantly across the professional groups (H(4) = 123.02, p

papers.title_zh: 土耳其一所大学医院医护人员的 HPV 知识、疫苗接种 的吸收和 疫苗接种 的障碍:一项横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Healthcare workers play a central role in human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination counselling and substantially influence vaccine acceptance. However, adequate theoretical knowledge does not necessarily translate into personal vaccination uptake or effective preventive behaviors. Objective This study aimed to assess HPV-related knowledge, personal HPV vaccination uptake, self-reported barriers to vaccination, and factors independently associated with HPV knowledge among healthcare workers at a university hospital in Türkiye. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at Süleyman Demirel University Research and Application Hospital between 15 December 2025 and 15 February 2026. A total of 288 healthcare workers participated in the study. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire and a 33-item Turkish HPV Knowledge Scale. Group differences were evaluated using Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests, followed by Dwass–Steel–Critchlow–Fligner post-hoc comparisons where appropriate. Effect sizes were reported as r and epsilon squared (ε2). Factors independently associated with total HPV knowledge scores were examined using multivariable linear regression with HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. Results The mean age of the participants was 36.38 ± 8.62 years, 70.1% were female, and 45.5% were physicians. The mean total HPV Knowledge Scale score was 24.62 ± 6.11 (out of 33). Knowledge gaps were particularly evident regarding vaccine availability and access, age-related indications, and male vaccination. Total knowledge scores differed significantly across the professional groups (H(4) = 123.02, p
